chapter: Joining Carter and Goodman in New York
title: Eddie Moore's sub band and how Hammond and Benny Carter found him
summary: Wilson subbed for Hines with Eddie Moore's band, was heard on the radio by John Hammond, and Carter and George Rich drove out and hired him.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Oh, let me see ... Benny Carter had heard about me from John Hammond. You see, if you had a good radio in New York in those days, you could hear Chicago, because see, when the Grand Terrace would broadcast, At midnight Chicago time, and when Earl would go on the Road, I would sub for Earl with the Eddie Moore band. I forgot to tell you about that.

Well, Clarence Moore was his name, but they called him Eddie Moore, and he had a sub band when Earl Hines was so famous in those days from his broadcast, he'd go on the road, and they got me to play because they knew I was sort of like a carbon copy of Earl on the piano. Because I sounded like Earl.

And that attracted them, so they got me to play there, and John Hammond heard me on the radio, because the New York stations -- when it's one o'clock in New York, they went off the air -- at the same time, we were coming on the air in Chicago at midnight. So John Hammond heard me, and he was already a friend of Benny Carter in New York and told Benny Carter about me.

So Benny Carter came out with his friend, George Rich, who was one of the richest racketeers in Harlem in those days, a very unusual man, and a real jazz fan and crazy about Benny Carter -- and the two of them came out in Rich's new Cadillac, and Benny Carter came and heard me, you know, and he liked what I was doing and hired me and then he hired Keg.
That's right. Keg got me the gig a few weeks later.
